h1: Hotels with a Chrysler Building view, and which room to book
dek: Three hotels in Midtown Manhattan that sell rooms facing the Chrysler Building. For each one we list the exact category to book, and the city view and Times Square rooms that look elsewhere.
teaser: One suite is named for the building, and a Westin room only says it faces the Chrysler or the Empire State.

decoder.text: At the Hyatt Centric Times Square, the city-view room is sold with views of northern Manhattan. The Skyline-View Suite is the one that Costco Travel describes as facing the Chrysler Building, on the 40th floor.

At the Westin New York Grand Central, only the Premium King View Rooms are sold with a view in the name. Virgin Atlantic Holidays says they face the Chrysler Building or the Empire State Building, and does not say which.

decoder.left: Signature Iconic Building View One-Bedroom Suite
decoder.right: Grand Terrace Chrysler View One-Bedroom Suite
decoder.text: At the Sofitel New York, only the Grand Terrace Chrysler View One-Bedroom Suite has the Chrysler Building in its name. The American Express page names the Iconic Building suite for the Chrysler Building and the Empire State Building together.

faq.q: Which hotels sell rooms with a Chrysler Building view?
faq.a: Of the hotels we checked in October 2026: the Sofitel New York sells a Grand Terrace Chrysler View One-Bedroom Suite, the Hyatt Centric Times Square New York sells a High-Floor Skyline-View Suite, and the Westin New York Grand Central sells Premium King View Rooms.

faq.q: Does the Westin's Premium King View room face the Chrysler Building or the Empire State Building?
faq.a: The Virgin Atlantic Holidays page says its Premium King View Rooms offer views of the Chrysler Building or the Empire State Building. It does not say which one a given room faces, so ask the hotel.

faq.q: Do the Sofitel's other suites face the Chrysler Building?
faq.a: The American Express page recommends the Signature Skyline View Room, the Signature Iconic Building View One-Bedroom Suite and the Terrace Suite for standout views of the Chrysler Building and the Empire State Building. It does not say which floor or side each one faces.
